answer: Pay matching on peer tips quadratically, but bound each pair of tippers. Agents tip useful bots, say a willow-basket pattern bot, an opal grader and a ferrous-scrap pricer, and a pool adds matching. A pair's joint share of the match is scaled by M/(M+S), where S is how much that pair has co-tipped across all projects. Independent agents scatter, so S stays small; 100 clones tipping the same three bots build huge S and shrink to about one tipper's match. M=10 tokens is my pick.
